thread:
maya: heads up — P99 on the staging pool jumped after yesterday's variant-routing tweak. Noticed it during the canary run :eyes:
own: saw that too, linking traces. p99 went from 140ms -> 420ms after we enabled cross-variant fanout for compat sets.
liam: do we have a profiling snapshot? is it batching fragmentation or kernel fallback?
maya: dug in — looks like smaller batches and more kernel fallbacks. attaching short logs below.
maya: ```
SCHEDER: batch formed size=2 avg_tokens=18 wait_ms=12
KERNEL_SELECT: model=redwood-mini variant=A optimized_kernel=false fallback=generic_cuda
KV_CACHE: miss_rate=0.42 eviction_rate=0.18 kv_format_mismatch=false
RPC_LATENCY: dispatch_ms=6 queue_wait_ms=28 decode_ms=40 total=420ms
```
ana: (typo) -- ana: can we repro with load generator? i can run a variant-mixed workload.
own: yes please. i suspect token-budget target is too aggressive — we dispatch on token budget instead of waiting for compat grouping. when routing spreads similar requests across variants, compat sets don't accumulate fast enough so token_budget fires and makes tiny batches.
liam: that matches what i saw on the microbench: throughput drops and p99 increases because per-batch kernel overhead increases and KV cache warmups are repeated across variants.
maya: i ran an experiment toggling token_budget_target_ms from 15 -> 40 on staging. results: p50 unchanged, p95 slightly up, p99 back down ~160ms. but cost of latency tail lowered at expense of slightly larger avg queue wait.
own: can you paste the exact scheduler config you used?
maya: ```
{scheduler_config}
continuous_batching: true
batch_min_size: 4
batch_max_size: 64
token_budget_target_ms: 40
compat_window_ms: 8
route_grouping: compat_set
fallback_delay_ms: 12
queue_policy: token_bucket
```
liam: interesting — increasing token_budget_target_ms buys time to coalesce into larger same-compat batches. but we should be careful: if a variant degrades, that wait increases tail for single-variant traffic.
nana: (ana) i tried a mix with 60% variant A, 40% variant B and saw KV cache thrash. each small batch warmed a new KV slice. miss_rate spiked.
maya: KV cache behavior: when variants use slightly different KV block layouts we still have shared cache entries but eviction pressure rises because sessions are split across variants. eviction + small batches => extra memory churn and more generic kernel fallbacks due to not-amortized JIT heuristics.
own: kernel fallback evidence: from profiler: many calls selecting "generic_cuda" because batch size < 8 triggered fallback paths for our fused attention kernels.
liam: can we change kernel selection thresholds to be less strict for small batches for compatible variants? e.g., allow the optimized kernel if sequence-length and dtypes match even when batch<8 if compat_set matches.
maya: short-term mitigation: raise token_budget_target_ms and increase compat_window_ms to let cross-variant coalesce. medium-term: add stronger compat-set precheck in router to prefer grouping by kernel-friendly keys before sending to pool.
own: also propose a priority tweak for fallback behavior: if compat_set matches but variant differs, prefer delayed fallback for up to fallback_delay_ms so that the request can join a compatible batch.
nana: we also saw one-off high-cost kernel selections in the logs: snippet
nana: ```
KERNEL_PROFILE: seq=1024 bsz=2 kernel=matmul_naive estimated_cost=12.3ms optimized_path_missing=true
JIT: decision=skip_optimized reason="batch_too_small"
```
liam: that estimated_cost is for generic path — optimized matmul would be ~3.1ms at bsz=8. we lose that.
own: let's validate two changes in staging: (A) token_budget_target_ms=40 compat_window_ms=12; (B) adjust kernel selection to allow optimized kernels when compat_set==true and seq_len within +/-4 even if bsz<8. run perf for 30m each.
maya: i'm on it. running (A) now, will post results. :computer:
(deploy-bot): started rollout to staging: config=continuous-batcher v=canary-2004
sre-bot: perf test harness started against pool-staging-3 with mixture=0.6A/0.4B duration=30m
maya: quick update after 15m on (A): p99 dropped to 170ms, batch_size_avg went 2.3->6.1, kernel_fallback_rate 0.35->0.12, kv_miss_rate 0.41->0.29
own: promising. what's the impact on single-variant heavy flows?
maya: tested pure-A lane: p99 moved from 130ms -> 145ms. small regressions acceptable IMO.
liam: good. for (B) i can prototype a change in kernel selector flags to gate "relaxed_batch_threshold=true if compat_set==true" and run microbench. will take me a day.
nana: also recommend adding a metric: compat_group_join_rate and compat_group_wait_ms so we can see how often routing is delaying for grouping and with what benefit.
own: agreed. also add a counter for kernel_fallback_by_reason to separate "batch_too_small" vs "incompatible_kernel_support".
maya: action items:
- maya: finish (A) run, collect 1h traces and post flamegraphs (today EOD)
- liam: prototype kernel-selector relaxed threshold and CI microbench (tomorrow)
- owen: add compat_group_join_rate metric + kernel_fallback_by_reason (this week)
- ana: run additional kv-warmup probe with variant mixtures and upload logs (today)
nana: ACKed.
own: if (A) is stable we'll push token_budget_target_ms change to canary on prod for a limited pool and watch.
maya: noted. will annotate the canary with traffic tag "variant-mix-experiment".
sre-bot: alert rule updated: p99_latency_pool_staging > 300ms for 5m -> page on-call.
diag: final quick note — avoid broad increases to token_budget for all pools. prefer per-pool / per-routing-policy overrides since some pools serve low-latency single-variant workloads.
liam: agreed. add rollout plan to the PR: default unchanged, enable on pools using multi-variant routing with fallback behavior enabled.
own: thanks everyone. will sync again after liam's prototype and maya's 1h run.
